title: Art: the craft of the encoding
summary: Metaphor domains as artistic medium — aesthetic choices that stay lossy, artful vocabularies, and examples that teach without pointing at real people.

blocks.title: Lossy on purpose, beautiful on purpose
blocks.body: Privacy craft and art craft meet in the vocabulary. The metaphor domain is not only a disguise — it is the medium. Choose domains that carry tone, pressure, and image while remaining generic. Stay fictional. Stay non-identifying. Make the page worth reading as prose, not only as a policy.

blocks.heading: Metaphor domains that tend to stay lossy
blocks.caption: Illustrative domains only — swap freely; never pin them to a real cast.
rows: Dependencies, delayed signals, veto points at the gate
Do not reuse one invented port across essays
Handoffs, timing, who hears the ticket
Slow failure, maintenance, weather as externality
Skip real farm or town tells
Roles, cues, one late entrance collapsing a phrase
Shared tools, weather windows, who carries the radio

blocks.heading: Aesthetic choices that earn their place
blocks.body:
Artful encoding picks concrete sensory detail that many lives could share: the smell of overheated dust, the sound of a radio that only one role carries, the way a line goes quiet before a stop. Those details are texture. They fail the art when they become unique: a scar, a license plate, a joke only six people tell.

Prefer image systems that are rich and common over image systems that are sparse and rare. A crowded metaphor domain hides you better and usually reads better.

items.label: Good texture
items.detail: "The ticket printer spat three orders before anyone looked up" — common kitchen pressure.

items.label: Too pointed
items.detail: "The ticket printer under the faded Packers schedule in Unit 4" — stacked quasi-identifiers.

items.label: Good domain shift
items.detail: Retell a plant-floor handoff as a harbor tug waiting on a signature from shore.

items.label: Bad continuity
items.detail: The same tug, same dock, same captain nickname across five essays.

blocks.heading: A short studio exercise
items: Take a mechanism you already encoded in plain roles.
Rewrite it once in a harbor domain and once in a kitchen domain.
Keep the falsifiable claim identical; only the costume changes.
Pick the version that is more vivid and still passes Rules 1–4.

blocks.title: Art does not suspend the underside
blocks.body: A beautiful allegory about data you should not have is still a violation with better lighting. Finish with the underside rule, then enjoy the craft.

blocks.quote: The best private allegory is specific to the reader who needed it and generic to everyone else — and still a pleasure to read.
